B.N. Chowdhury with G.G. Shaha ----- For the Petitioner.

parties:
Sultanuddin Chowdhury ----- Petitioner.
Vs.
Government of the People's Republic of Bangladesh and others ----- Respondents.
full_judgment: 3. In the foregoing facts and circumstances of the case the petitioner's valid purchase of the property from the said Sushil Kumar Gangali remains undisputed uptil now. This is quite evident from the order passed on 15.3.77 by Mr. M.A. Samad, Joint Secretary, Ministry of Land Administration and Land Reforms of the Government of Bangladesh, wherein it was held that the petitioner's property was never listed as a vested property nor was it made khas property of the Government. In such circumstances it was further ordered that it was not necessary to treat the property in question to be under any unauthorized possession of the petitioner and on that account the petitioner's eviction was avoided. It is surprising to note that only after four months on 22.7.77 another order was passed by Mr. So. Hossain Khan, Joint Secretary in the Ministry of Land Administration and Reforms of the Government of Bangladesh wherein it was held that the property in question appeared to have been held as vested property and on 15.3.77 was reviewed and revised. In passing the subsequent order of 22.7.77 it was observed that the petitioner's title in the property in question was doubtful. Apart from the act that the petitioner's title is based upon valid purchase of the property by a duly registered deed. The authority in the Government could not question and annul the validity of such title by an executive order. If the Government wanted to claim in such property it could only do so by way of an appropriate suit for declaration of title and cancellation of the petitioner's registered kabala as such. Be that as it may it is surprising to note that a Joint Secretary in the Ministry of Land Reforms could revise an order passed only four months before by his predecessor, another Joint Secretary in the said Ministry of land Administration and Land Reforms. The subsequent order passed by Joint Secretary Mr. S. Hossain Khan on 22.7.77 is obviously based on illegal assumption of fact and as such suffers from clear illegality. The said impugned order being marked as Annexure B to the petition is accordingly set aside.
